topics.topic: Where caller pre-publication requirements should be documented
questions: Move the requirements that callers invoke put_value_bytes and spool_file before record_change to the notes of the respective callers/callsites, leaving the record_change note to state only its own preconditions and behavior.

Move the requirements that the caller invoke put_value_bytes and spool_file before record_change to the notes of each caller/callsite; keep this record_change note limited to record_change's own handling of records and its prohibition on publishing or re-checking bytes.

quotes: record_change: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] A StoredValue whose value_id already exists is not written again, since equal values share one identity. A StoredValue carries no bytes: the bytes of every StoredValue a change names MUST already be published under its value_digest by the caller with put_value_bytes before the change, as spooled files must already be published in the run's spool by spool_file before the change that writes their SpooledFile records; record_change publishes, rewrites and re-checks no value bytes and no spooled file, and writes only records.
judgement.why: The note assigns callers the callsite orchestration of invoking put_value_bytes and spool_file before record_change, but §2 requires such a call-boundary requirement to be owned by the caller or callsite.
judgement.rule: Владелец такой ноты — caller/callsite, не callee.

topics.topic: How to classify and separate the pre-publication, file-access, and field-assignment requirements
questions: The pre-publication and no-file-access requirement must use [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] as its primary class; keep the existing-record assignment rule in a separate [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] note if both requirements are retained.

quotes: record_change: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] A StoredValue whose value_id already exists is not written again, since equal values share one identity. A StoredValue carries no bytes: the bytes of every StoredValue a change names MUST already be published under its value_digest by the caller with put_value_bytes before the change, as spooled files must already be published in the run's spool by spool_file before the change that writes their SpooledFile records; record_change publishes, rewrites and re-checks no value bytes and no spooled file, and writes only records.
judgement.why: The note's stronger behavioral role concerns publication and file access, so classifying the combined requirement as FIELD_ASSIGNMENT does not select its primary semantic class.
judgement.rule: Если note смешивает несколько ролей, выбери primary class по смыслу, потеря которого сильнее изменит generated behavior. Не расщепляй note механически ради классификации, если это только ухудшает читаемость.

topics.topic: Whether record_change or its callers are responsible for publishing value and spooled files
questions: Must value and spooled files be published by record_change as part of the change, or must they be published by callers before record_change so that a failed change merely leaves previously published files unnamed?

quotes: record_change: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] A StoredValue whose value_id already exists is not written again, since equal values share one identity. A StoredValue carries no bytes: the bytes of every StoredValue a change names MUST already be published under its value_digest by the caller with put_value_bytes before the change, as spooled files must already be published in the run's spool by spool_file before the change that writes their SpooledFile records; record_change publishes, rewrites and re-checks no value bytes and no spooled file, and writes only records.

record_change: [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] Durability order: every file a change names is published, fsynced and its directory fsynced before the change is committed, and the SQLite database runs with synchronous FULL, so after a power loss a committed record never names a missing or partial file; a file published by a change that then failed stays unnamed: a value file until the next start removes it, a spooled file until it is replaced at its position or its run's spool is removed (A18 rule 4).
judgement.why: The texts explicitly require callers to publish both kinds of files before record_change, forbid record_change from publishing them, and specify that a failed change leaves those files unnamed.

topics.topic: Semantics of None for a missing versus explicitly empty required_headers field
questions: Must a missing required_headers field be projected as None, or is None permitted only when the instance explicitly states none?

quotes: read_service_record: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST project the record into ManifestServiceRecord: instances is an object keyed by instance name, so an instance's key in instances becomes instance_name and its class becomes instance_class; an instance's required_headers is an object mapping each header name to its value, as platform manifest records write it, and becomes the tuple of one HeaderField per entry with both texts verbatim, in the record's order, None when the instance states none; exposed_as http_api given as one string, a list or absent becomes the tuple of its routes, and each capability's record_digest is content_identity of the canonical JSON of that one raw capability entry; effect_class stays text.
judgement.divergence: One implementer projects an absent required_headers field as None, while another projects it as an empty tuple or refuses the record because only an explicitly stated none permits None; callers receiving ManifestInstance or ManifestOperation notice the different value or refusal.
judgement.why: The passage specifies explicit objects and instances that state none but does not determine the projection of a missing required_headers field.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
